answer.summary: Pfeffer says breaking conventional rules can make a person or business memorable and help it stand apart from incumbents who benefit from the existing rules. Success comes from doing something different that plays to your strengths and helps you succeed—not from rule-breaking for its own sake.

sections.heading: Why it can work
sections.content: Unexpected behavior makes you stand out and become memorable. Pfeffer also argues that rules are often made by people favored by the status quo, so departing from convention can open a path to disruption. At the individual level, he advises choosing actions that play to your strengths, distinguish you, and improve your chances of success.

sections.heading: Examples Pfeffer gives
sections.content: In business, he cites Southwest not using hub-and-spoke, Amazon emphasizing exceptional customer service, and Whole Foods fitting local tastes rather than optimizing only for cost. For an individual example, he describes Jason Calacanis as defying venture-capital conventions: making many small bets rather than a few big ones, running lean, and having no partners. Pfeffer also says that asking for help can defy the convention of appearing self-sufficient; people tend to overestimate how many people they must ask, and asking can feel uncomfortable.
